chapter: Army, return to El Paso and Mardi Gras parades
title: Induction into the Army and a year at home after discharge
summary: Watts was inducted at Shreveport, did basic training at Camp Harahan in New Orleans, and after discharge worked a few nights at jitney dance halls.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: You never did play any parades around here? When you came back from Fort Worth?
No, until I came back, until I was discharged out to Army.

45, not then. Then Alfred Williams, they heard that I was back here, you see. And I had been out there playing at George's, that's why I first got my greetings from Uncle Sam, see. Oh yeah. And I was just to be allowed to come to Shreeport because I had some people living in Shreeport. See. And at the time I had a girl that I was very fond of at that time, see, in Shreeport. So they gave me permission to go to Fort Humburg in Shreeport to be inducted, see. And so I cut on back down there to Shreeport. And then, after taking my examination and spending the night at the Veteran Hospital there for that spinal tap, well I was allowed, I was allowed to come to, at least to be fortunate enough to be sent home. Now at that time, before I got Norman, I was away from New Orleans for 12 years. See, well, they sent me home right to Camp Harahan, right out here in New Orleans. And usually they send me, you know, someone they inducted away from home to get them used to being away from his people, see. But they sent me right home for my basic training and I spent 17 weeks right out here in Camp Harahan taking my basics, see. But I didn't do any playing. I came out home in 45, I stayed a year around here. Oh, I played a few places. At that time the Foyne was running, that's the Jitney dance on Iberville Street there, between Ramport and Burgundy, the Foyne, and then they had another one, the La Vida. Well, Lee Collin was playing at the, I think, one or the other, the La Vida if I'm not mistaken, and Anderson, this boy who I played, who hires me every year to play this parade with his brass band, he was playing at the Foyne, or Vice Versus. And see, and Anderson would lay off a couple of nights a week because it was such a tough job, you know, the Jitney dance. And he let me work a couple of nights in his place. And then I used to go in some nights that I wasn't working, and I always like, Lee Collin's and I always been good friends. And I'd go in, as soon as I'd walk in, you know, he wanted to go down by the E-Light, you remember the old E-Light restaurant where the musicians used to gather on Ramport Street, he wanted to go down there and get a bite to eat, you know, about 10, 30, 11 o'clock.
